Aggressive Description: Aggressive measures the intensity, harshness, and physical impact of the audio.
All songs will be played at a normalized: All songs will be played at a normalized volume.
Arousal Description: The physiological and psychological state of being awake or reactive to stimuli, ranging from sleep to excitement.
Author: Author
Engagement Description: Engagement measures how much a track grabs the listener’s attention, primarily through rhythmic stability, percussive strength, and predictability.
Happy Description: Happy identifies music with high valence (emotional positivity). It looks for acoustic signals that humans associate with joy, safety, and celebration.
Name: Name
Party Description: Party is heavily influenced by the presence of a steady, synthetic, or highly compressed kick drum and a repetitive rhythmic structure.
Relaxed Description: Relaxed measures the lack of tension and physical calmness in the music.
Sad Description: Sad measures the emotional weight and low valence of a track. It is closely linked to Melancholy and is often the acoustic opposite of Happy.

Tonal Description: Tonal music revolves around a tonic (a home note). It follows established scales and keys that the human ear finds predictable and generally pleasant.
Tour BPM Widget: This helps you match the "heartbeat" of your session. If the party is in a high-speed chase,turn the dial up to filter for high Beats Per Minute (BPM) tracks to keep the energy high.
Tour Category Slider: Use these to fine-tune your search. If your party is entering a legendary cathedral, crank up the Mysticismand Heroism. The list below will automatically filter for tracks that meet these specific intensity levels.
Tour Directory Tree: This is your source for all music. Click a folder to load all contained songs intothe main table, or click a single file to play it instantly. Use this to organize your different campaign locations(e.g., Tavern Music,Combat,Stealth). You can also set a new home directory to make navigation faster.
Tour Effectslist: These are your layering sounds. Open a directory containing you effects and click an effect to start it. These run independently of your music, allowing you to have a'Tavern' song playing in the main player while 'Rain' or 'Bonfire' crackle in the background for extra immersion.
Tour Menubar: Feeling a bit overwhelmed? Tailor the app to your screen size or DMing style. Under this menu, you can hide orshow most widgets (like the Mood Map or Effects Rack). If you only need the Track List during a session, hide everything elseto create a clean, distraction-free interface.
Tour Presets Widget: Once you’ve dialed in the perfect mix of sliders, BPM, and Mood Map coordinates, you don't want to lose it!Type a name into the box (like 'Epic Boss' or 'Spooky Cave') and click the Save icon. You can now instantly recall thoseexact filter settings later by selecting them from the dropdown, allowing you to change the entire atmosphere of your roomin one click.
Tour Russel Widget: This is the heart of the app. Drag the blue dot to find music that matchesthe current emotional beat of your game. Want something tense for a boss? Drag it toward Angry/Excited.Want a peaceful town theme? Move it toward Happy/Relaxed.
Tour Song Table: This shows the songs currently available based on your filters. Double-click a row to play a song, or glance at the tags to see ifit’s 'Sad' or 'Energetic'. Right click non the headers to customize their visibility.
Tour Tags Widget: These are one-click filters. Use them to quickly narrow down your library by genre or instrument.For example, toggle Drums and Dark to instantly find percussive combat tracks.
